user.title: Plooum CamRecorder
user.description: Saves photos and videos of your cameras on the Home Assistant server, from dashboards, automations and scripts.

data_description.folder: Where photos and videos are saved, one subfolder per camera. Must be a media folder (or inside allowlist_external_dirs) to show in the media browser.
data_description.keep_days: Files older than this are deleted. 0: kept forever.
data_description.max_size_gb: Above this, the oldest files are deleted. 0: no limit.
data_description.cameras: These cameras get a Take photo button, a Recording switch and Last photo / Last video sensors. The actions work with every camera anyway.

error.not_allowed: Home Assistant may not write there: use a media folder or add it to allowlist_external_dirs.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Plooum CamRecorder is already set up: change its options instead.

snapshot.name: Take photo
snapshot.description: Saves a photo of the cameras on the server. Responds with the saved files.

record.name: Record video
record.description: Records a video of the cameras on the server and waits until it is saved. Responds with the saved files. The camera needs a stream.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Length of the video, lookback not included.

lookback.name: Lookback
lookback.description: Seconds before the call to include. Only when the camera's stream already runs (Preload stream, or someone watching).

start_recording.name: Start recording
start_recording.description: Starts a video of the cameras, stopped by Stop recording or after the maximum duration. The camera needs a stream.

max_duration.name: Maximum duration
max_duration.description: The video stops by itself after this long.

lookback.name: Lookback
lookback.description: Seconds before the call to include. Only when the camera's stream already runs (Preload stream, or someone watching).

stop_recording.name: Stop recording
stop_recording.description: Stops the videos of the cameras and waits until they are saved. Responds with the saved files.
